purpose: Real result of dispatching .github/workflows/fda-approval.yml for the first time, for NDA020793 (CAFCIT / caffeine citrate, sponsor HIKMA) -- the same real Drugs@FDA application tests/test_fda_approvals.py and tests/test_fda_ingestion.py already use as ground truth.
context: Like ClinicalTrials.gov (reports/m3-clinical-trial-workflow-result-2026-09-30.json) and unlike Milestone 3 Phase B's earnings-surprise pipeline (data.sec.gov's own paths confirmed blocked from GitHub Actions with HTTP 403, reports/m3-earnings-surprise-workflow-result-2026-09-30.json), openFDA's drugsfda.json endpoint succeeded on the very first real dispatch -- matching what local testing already predicted before any code was written. This is the second Milestone 3 capability confirmed genuinely runnable end to end against live data from GitHub Actions, not just code-complete.
not_a_claim: Not a claim about CAFCIT's own clinical or commercial significance -- 'approved' describes each submission's own regulatory status only.

Not a general claim that every openFDA path is unblocked -- only this specific endpoint (drug/drugsfda.json, searched by application_number) has been confirmed working from GitHub Actions so far. submission_class_code's own larger, fragmented enum is deliberately not classified yet (nre/fda_approvals.py's own module docstring).

Not a claim that this project's own 23 accepted issuers have FDA-approved products in Drugs@FDA -- several smaller/clinical-stage biotech issuers searched during this phase returned no matches, consistent with Drugs@FDA covering only approved applications. NDA020793 was used as an independently verifiable ground-truth example, not as one of this project's own issuers.
